The visually inspected ADIB consolidated income statement, physical page 4, reports total six-month profit of EGP7,550,833 thousand, of which EGP7,536,797 thousand belongs to bank shareholders. Their difference is EGP14,036 thousand, agreeing with the non-controlling-interest line. The shareholder amount is the relevant earnings scope when assessing the bank's ordinary equity; total group profit includes earnings attributable to other owners. It is not the separate bank-only profit.

The small net ECL charge of EGP2,176 thousand is helpful to current reported earnings, but it is a flow after releases and charges, not a stock measure of asset quality. The same page's EGP78,142 thousand second-quarter release demonstrates netting across time. Strong positive funding income is supportive, while missing stage balances, impaired-financing ratios, collateral, coverage, write-offs and provision assumptions prevent a clean-loan conclusion. Recoveries or model changes could influence net ECL, but the page does not establish that either occurred. A bank valuation needs sustainable attributable earnings, capital adequacy, distributions and valuation inputs as well as credit quality. Decision: keep the earnings scope correct, request the financing-quality and capital schedules, and wait on any investment recommendation; do not interpret a low charge as evidence of no risk.
